correctness.rationale: For H=M⊕N with M=Ce0 and N=ell2, K=P_M and U=I_M⊕B with B the backward unilateral shift, U is onto, commutes with K, leaves R(K)^perp invariant and is noninjective (ker U=C f1). The one-atom family Φ=(e0) is a Parseval K-frame: its coefficient square equals ||K*f||². UΦ=UP_MΦ=Φ; none of these singleton families permits removal, so all three deletion excesses equal zero. This directly contradicts the iff global-injectivity assertion of Corollary 5.11 despite satisfying its printed assumptions. For the corrected restricted statement, the relevant ordinary projected frame lies in M; on V=U|M the synthesis-kernel exact sequence of a surjective V gives dim ker(VT)=dim ker T+dim ker V, in finite-excess cases. The visible excess can detect only ker(U|M), never a kernel solely in M-perp. Critically, this argument does NOT assume the false unrestricted equality E_K(Φ)=E(P_MΦ) in general; it holds here because all atoms are in M. All steps are exact infinite-dimensional operator identities, not finite approximations.
